name: 2024-08-26 Commissioning Plan
description:
AuxTel 
Standard AuxTel night with standard calibrations and scheduled driven observation.

The highest priority for the night should be the scheduler-driven observations. Please try to complete the daytime calibrations tests if time allows. If you need to skip or interrupt the daytime calibrations in order to go on-sky on time with the scheduler-driven survey, that is okay.

For the daytime calibrations, if the WREB does not reach the temperature range needed in time to complete them before going on-sky (see Step 1 here https://obs-ops.lsst.io/AuxTel/Standard-Operations/Daytime-Operations/latiss-combined-calibrations-procedure.html), they can be skipped.

Simonyi Telescope
We also want to run a couple of tests with Simonyi to remind ourselves how things work and to review part of the workflow of data collection.
The tests added here should be executed only when AuxTel is already on Sky and running with the Scheduler.
We will have little/no support. If there is any problem that seems to hard to solve put the system into a safe state, stop the tests, and file an OBS ticket.

Once you are done with the tests associated with MainTel, put every component in their original state.

customFields.End of Night - Current CSC Status: Only MT2 Hexapod warm up (BLOCK-T3) was done. No CamHexapod available for tonight. Thus the scheduled observing blocks BLOCK-T4, BLOCK-T88 were skipped.

Freddy will coordinate this activity, with OS Team supporting TMA operations. Be prepared to start it around 16:00 LT. Priori to that, the electronics team will turn the OSS ON and prepare the TMA cabinets to power up the drives. They will also conduct the regular walk around, and then handover TMA operations to the observers. They may need help from the OS team with walk around.

If time permits, after balancing, execute hexapods and laser tracker test cases. 
They should be executed only (1) after balancing is finished and (2) when AuxTel is already on Sky and running with the Scheduler.

Once you are done with the tests associated with MainTel, put every used component in their original state (see BLOCK-T139).

customFields.End of Night - Current CSC Status:
Simonyi Telescope
We began the hexapods startup at 11:30 CLT, which passed without any issues. We then continued with the M2 and Camera hexapod warm-ups, which also completed successfully without any problems. Late afternoon we attempted to turn on the MTRotator but were hindered with interlocks being triggered. Restarting the MTRotator control system took some time but we were able to ENABLE the MTRotator shortly after. The plan was to conduct a minimum functionality test with MTRotator (BLOCK-T164). However, CCW was unavailable due to an E-stop and BLOCK-T164 could not be executed. We however improvised and conducted minimum motion functionality test of MTRotator through the CSC using a specific version of MTPtg : these involved moving the MTRotator within +/- 1.5 deg in steps of 0.5 deg using the move_rotator script. All of these were successful.

Rest of the night was focussed on running Cam Hexapod workouts for almost 4 hours. Throughout the workout, the strut temperatures rose and remained stable at ~19.8 deg C. MTM2 tangential link temperature however displayed erratic behaviour with fluctuations and slight rise in temperature. This stopped when the Cam Hexapod workout finished. We also had some recurring  "MTForceError.MTM2" alarms.

Final telescope status:
MTRotator, MTHexapod.1 & 2 in STANDBY and the cabinets/PXI shutdown; MTMount DISABLED and M1M3 ENABLED

AuxTel
We started the day with the AuxTel daytime checkouts at 10:21 CLT. The Latiss_checkout failed with a timeout: waiting for imageInOODS event for bias frame, we ran it again and passed. During the slew_and_take_image script, LATISS failed again, subsequently, both the ATMCS and ATPtg systems failed, leading us to recycle those components and then ran the point_azel script to correct the slewing. The daytime checkout was completed after that, although we skipped the venting procedure due to high winds (above 8 m/s). We then proceeded with the daytime calibrations, where the white lamp turned on at the first attempt and passed with minor issues. We started the first of three linearity scans, but encountered a failure related to the ATMonochromator being in STANDBY, which should have been set to ENABLE in a prior step. Upon rerunning the BLOCK, it failed again, and the ATMonochromator went into FAULT. Parkr rebooted the ATMonochromator, and we reran BLOCK-271_1, but received anoth
er timeo
ut error. This appeared to be a DDS error. After trying once more, the process worked successfully. The linearity scans Part 2 was successful in the second attempt while part 3 finished successfully in the first go. 

The night started a bit cloudy with some repeat errors with correct pointing, latiss_take_sequence. A recycling of ATPtg followed by correct_pointing script helped resolve them and rest of the night was smooth. We got ~ 5 hrs of on-sky time with better skies towards the end. We decided to close AuxTel for the night after an OODS time-out error.

Final telescope status:
Telescope and Dome in parked position; LATISS in STANDBY

  • Leak detector installation inside M1M3 cell

We want to push the walkaround to start early but given the amount of activities, we can expect a delay.
In addition, Freddy confirmed during the morning meeting that we can move the Camera Cable Wrap (CCW).

If everything goes well, here is the overall plan to go on Sky.
The night sequence is reflected in the sequence of the test cases in the Test Player.
Here is a summary:
  • We should start with system checks as soon as possible.
    This includes all the test cases marked as `2. Late Afternoon` or `3. Early Night` in the Environment.
  • We should execute the test cases BLOCK-T88 and BLOCKT-T222 should only if we cannot go on sky.
    Mark them as skipped if otherwise.
  • Telescope park/unpark - only run this at the end of the night. 

Freeform Test
  • Depending on the situation, we might not move the telescope at all.
    In that case, there is value in opening the dome shutter and monitor the temperatures in the Glycol Performance vs Ambient Dashboard.
    This will allow us gathering data to better understand the risks of opening the dome without having the M1M3 TS.
    See the "Reminders" below for criteria about when to close the dome.

Reminders
  • We are limited to move the telescope at 1% its maximum velocity, acceleration, and jerk.
    This affects where we want to point in the sky.
    Any movement with the telescope will take a long time.
  • We still need to verify the pointing model.
    The telescope tracking might not be accurate so slow moving targets are ideal
  • When leaving the parking position at Zenith, move the telescope to ~ 80º before homing.
    This is associated with a "false" homing that happens when trying to home near Zenith.

    This means that the project mandates that we have targets only pointing towards South and West.

This is mostly associated with the dome seeing and will give you hints for when we should power off the HVAC system and open the dome shutter.

name: LSSTCam stray light and ghost verification
description:
This test cycle collects the test cases for stray light investigations and verification with LSSTCam. The tests lead to the collection of different datasets at nighttime on-sky and daytime with the CBP.
The analysis of the data will be reported in a homologue test campaign of the LVV project.

name: 2025-04-11 to 2025-04-13 Commissioning Plan
description:
Before going on, make sure you review the Temporary Guidelines - LSSTCam on-sky (DRAFT).

name: 2025-04-14 Commissioning Plan
description:
The camera CCDs were turned on today, but the HV Bias will be turned on tomorrow. It is not possible to go on-sky tonight.
Additionally, the dome will remain locked out due to an ongoing issue.
Before going on, make sure you review the Temporary Guidelines - LSSTCam on-sky (DRAFT). 

The general flow of activities will be:
  • In Dome work on Calibration System
  • Dome Shutter tests (as part of dome handover)
  • Move to Zenith early in the night and perform the following:
    • Move TMA to Zenith, perform Rotator tests
    • Filter Elevation test under CCS
  • When camera testing is complete, around midnight:
    • TMA Soak test at 10%

These are the tests we would like to run during April 14, 2025:

  • T382 Acquire Biases
  • T412 Acquire Darks

  • T370 Filter Elevation Scan CCS control
  • T437 TMA Soak test (mtdome closed) - Without LSSTCam

name: 2025-08-13 Commissioning Plan
description:
Must read pages
  • Temporary Guidelines - LSSTCam on-sky
  • SITCOM Test Planning - Canvas with the priorities of the Week

Weather, Sun, and Moon 
  • Sunset: 18:17 CLT / 22:17 UTC
  • Nautical Twilight End (-12 deg solar elevation): 19:10 CLT / 23:10 UTC. 
  • Sunrise: 07:17 CLT / 11:17 UTC
  • Moon: Illumination 77.9%, Moonrise: 23:05 CLT, Moonset: 10:22 (next day) CLT.
  • Weather forecast (mountain-forecast): Clear skies, warmish weather
  
The dome should be moved to East and open at sunset for venting. 

New dashboard for image vignetting (embargo data or not for calibration): https://summit-lsp.lsst.codes/chronograf/sources/1/dashboards/608?refresh=Paused&lower=now%28%29%20-%201h
When taking calibration data, stop if not fully vignetted. Problem must be fixed before continuing.

Plan Summary
Filters: griz

AOS: Highest OnSky Priority 
Enable hexapods with LUT_update_positive.yaml and enable compensation (see #summit-control-room)
  • BLOCK-T393_v5: Long closed loop LUT
  • BLOCK-T598: Sensitivity Matrix Repeatability
  • BLOCK-T395_v5: FAM rotator scan

SV in the second half of the night:
  • BLOCK-T544: SV survey
    • This can be used as a validation for the AOS updates.
    • Only if we are able to close the loop with AOS

On-Sky Stray Light Tests:
These can be done if it is too cloudy outside to close the AOS (These tests use a very bright star). Otherwise skip them.
  • BLOCK-T596 (35 mins)
  • BLOCK-T599 (40 mins)

End of night:
  • BLOCK-T399v3: Daily Cals (uses new version of BLOCk-T495. Revert to older version if something goes wrong)

If you have to close the dome early:
  • In order of priority:
    • BLOCK-597 : the M2 baffle + CBP measurement in Y band wavelength (no filter) (90min)
    • BLOCK-T556: Whitelight Flats (run for all installed filters) (90 minutes)
    • BLOCK-T593: M1M3 thermalization test

____________________________________________________________________________________
Homing the axes with home_both_axes.py script

  • To improve homing accuracy and ensure axes homing is done at a consistent az/el location, we have added a feature to the home_both_axes.py script that will first home the axes in its current location (as usual), then slew the TMA to a fixed position in az/el and perform the homing again. This should be run every time you need to home the axes, including after recovering from a TMA fault. Note that the MTPtg Component must be ENABLED in order to command the slew to the final home position. 

  • The feature can be enabled by adding the following configuration to the home_both_axes.py script:
    We want to keep the position az:1, el: 46 for this. This position was chosen as it is in the middle of both axes ranges. 


final_home_position: 
  az: 1 
  el: 46

Dome Warming Procedure:
  1. Close dome
  2. Set HVAC setpoints to high (15-20C)
  3. Also have @Petr Kubánek or @Brian Stalder online to adjust the M1M3 setpoint - Need to confirm with Petr that it is working as expected, but some automation is in place. 
  4. CAVEAT: Once we are closed due to cold weather (and heating the dome), even if it warms up OUTSIDE, we do NOT re-open the dome for on-sky that same night

M1M3 status
  • Need to move TMA in 5% speed using EUI if mirror is lowered.
  • Mirror raising/lowering
  • Raising the mirror can be done for El > 20 deg
  • Lowering the mirror can be done El > 45 deg (due to OBS-1038)
  • M1M3 switched back to "enabled HP corrections after raise"
  • 10% GGGR
  • When M1M3 faults during the test, run bump test -> HP breakaway test again before raising mirror again

name: 2025-09-19 Commissioning Plan
description:
Must read pages
  • Temporary Guidelines - LSSTCam on-sky
  • SITCOM Test Planning - Canvas with the priorities of the Week

Weather, Sun, and Moon 
  • Sunset: 19:37 CLT / 22:37  UTC.
  • Nautical Twilight End (-12 deg solar elevation): 20:29 CLT / 23:29 UTC. 
  • Sunrise: 07:35 CLT / 10:35 UTC.
  • Moon: Illumination 5%, Moonset: 17:47 CLT, Moonrise: 06:27 CLT, 
  • Weather forecast (mountain-forecast): expect mild to cold temperatures for tonight. 
    Windy models present temperatures around ~10-13 ºC to start the night (meteoblue is the outlier, giving 5 ºC). 
    Mountain forecast says  we may start the night with ~7ºC (dropping to ~2ºC by the end of the night). Winds ~40 km/h. 
    Most models predict that we might have some clouds tonight.    

Confirm the below  
Check the M2Hexapod acceleration before going on sky.  Should be 250 microns/s^2. Check this dashboard.
 
The dome should be moved to East and open at sunset for venting. 

New dashboard for image vignetting (embargo data or not for calibration): 
https://summit-lsp.lsst.codes/chronograf/sources/1/dashboards/608?refresh=Paused&lower=now%28%29%20-%201h
When taking calibration data, stop if not fully vignetted. Problem must be fixed before continuing.

Scheduler - runs out of targets (something is wrong, not normal).  ask for support to verify the cause.
____________________________________________________________________________________
Reminder
If M1M3, M2, or Hexapods go into fault during on-sky observations:
  1. Enable CSCs and Hexapod Compensation Mode.
  2. Critically important: Run set_dof using a previous image with good image quality.
____________________________________________________________________________________
Plan Summary - On Sky
For the night, the weather forecast shows that we can go on sky although with some clouds. Keep an eye in the wind.
The DIMM should be ready for tonight, keep an eye on it from time to time. 
Double check it closes as expected at the end of the night.

Both SV and AOS are the main priority, however AOS get more on-sky time.
Run SV surveys ideally 60 min before 06:00 UTC each night. Even 20 min of observations is useful. After running AV, go back to AOS:

 - BLOCK-T395: Rotator LUT
 - BLOCK-T621: Hartmann style sensitivity matrix (large donut) going through 22 DOFs
 - BLOCK-T606: sensitivity matrix at non-zero rotation
- BLOCK-559: checking z-offsets for filter changes

Consider start with AOS, find a break point to run SV, then go back to AOS until the end of the night. If going on-sky gets delayed, starts with SV.
Note: AOS can tolerate more cloud coverage than SV. 

In case of poor conditions (bad seeing, not cloudy): 
- On-sky stray light test – can utilize poor conditions targeting Saturn:
  BLOCK-T599 (40min) stray light from filter shiny part with Saturn (on-sky).

We don't need to handover the dome to EIE over the weekend, so please, remember Daily Cals. 

The sequence of the tests in the Test Player define the priority for the tests. 
Comments are on each specific test execution.


Plan Summary - Closed Dome
Closed dome tests remain the same: 
For Monochromatic Flats, please run i-band and z-band filters. 
This is the highest closed-dome priority, followed by stray light tests.
Both require dark time (Sun below -5 deg should be dark enough).

Note that going on sky gets priority (abandon it if sky gets clear while taking flats).

Stray Light in-dome tests available:
- BLOCK-T610 (2h) stray light from from M2 baffle at 12 deg off-axis with CBP (in-dome)
- BLOCK-T611 (40min) stray light from autochanger with CBP (in-dome)
- BLOCK-T612 (40min) stray light from filter holder plate with CBP (in-dome)

M1M3 tests are lower priority than calibrations and stray light. 
However, they can be ran during the day. 
Run with 20%, only GGGG.
Follow the sequence of tests in the Test Player. 

Note: no need to repeat BLOCK-T6171.0M1M3 Z-Momement w/ different slew flags tonight.

Other Status
  • Filters available: griz
  • For tonight, we are using the following configuration for CamHex and M2Hexapod:  
    CameraHex: lut_version_0813.yaml
    M2Hex: lut_version_0813.yaml


____________________________________________________________________________________
Homing the axes with home_both_axes.py script

  • To improve homing accuracy and ensure axes homing is done at a consistent az/el location,
    we have added a feature to the home_both_axes.py script that will first home the axes in its current location (as usual),
    then slew the TMA to a fixed position in az/el and perform the homing again.
    This should be run every time you need to home the axes, 
    including after recovering from a TMA fault. 
    Note that the MTPtg Component must be ENABLED in order to command the slew to the final home position. 

  • The feature can be enabled by adding the following configuration to the home_both_axes.py script:
    We want to keep the position az:1, el: 46 for this.
    This position was chosen as it is in the middle of both axes ranges. 


final_home_position: 
  az: 1 
  el: 46

Dome Warming Procedure:
  1. Close dome
  2. Set HVAC setpoints to high (15 - 20C)
  3. Also have @Petr Kubánek or @Brian Stalder online to adjust the M1M3 setpoint. 
    Need to confirm with Petr that it is working as expected, but some automation is in place. 
  4. CAVEAT: Once we are closed due to cold weather (and heating the dome), 
    even if it warms up OUTSIDE, we do NOT re-open the dome for on-sky that same night

M1M3 status
  • Need to move TMA in 5% speed using EUI if mirror is lowered.
  • Mirror raising/lowering
  • Raising the mirror can be done for El > 20 deg
  • Lowering the mirror can be done El > 45 deg (due to OBS-1038)
  • M1M3 switched back to "enabled HP corrections after raise"
  • 10% GGGR
  • When M1M3 faults during the test, run bump test -> HP breakaway test again before raising mirror again

customFields.Requests for the end of the night: TMA pointing request will be pointing to HORIZON for all the Fiestas Patrias including Monday Sept 22nd. [David J Sept 17 2025]

name: 2025-10-20 Pre-Ops Campaign Plan
description:
Must read pages
  • Temporary Guidelines - LSSTCam on-sky
  • SITCOM Test Planning - Canvas with the priorities of the Week

Weather, Sun, and Moon 
  • Sunset: 19:57 CLT / 22:57  UTC.
  • Nautical Twilight End (-12 deg solar elevation): 20:50 CLT / 11:50 UTC 
  • Astronomical Twilight Start (-18 deg solar elevation): 05:35 CLT / 8:35 UTC 
  • Sunrise: 06:57 CLT / 9:57 UTC.
  • Moon: Illumination 1%, Moonset: 19:57 CLT, Moonrise: 06:19 CLT, 
  • Weather forecast (mountain-forecast): expect clear sky, mild wind, warming conditions.


Confirm the below  
Check the M2Hexapod acceleration before going on sky.  Should be 100 microns/s^2. Check this dashboard.

For this week, we will vent (shutter+E1 louver) for a minimum of 30 minutes before going on-sky. We will open and vent facing the wind around sunset (as soon as it is safe to point the telescope in that direction).    


New dashboard for image vignetting (determines whether data is embargoed or not for calibration): 
https://summit-lsp.lsst.codes/chronograf/sources/1/dashboards/608?refresh=Paused&lower=now%28%29%20-%201h
When taking calibration data, stop if not fully vignetted. Problem must be fixed before continuing.

Scheduler - runs out of targets (something is wrong, not normal).  ask for support to verify the cause.
____________________________________________________________________________________
Reminder
If M1M3, M2, or Hexapods go into fault during on-sky observations:
  1. Enable CSCs and Hexapod Compensation Mode.
  2. Critically important: Run set_dof using a previous image with good image quality.

____________________________________________________________________________________

Night conditions

"Soft Start" of pre-operations.  Camera will be in degraded conditions (only 2 filters available: i, z plus pinhole).  Close 1 hour before twilight (4:35 CLT) to do calibrations. AOS is highest priority.


Plan Summary

Take biases and darks as soon as you possibly can once the camera is turned on.


Start venting as soon as the sun sets (BLOCK-T464). Vent pointing to the wind. Open the louver and leave it open all night (BLOCK-T618).
  1. After handover, move immediately to zenith for filter testing (< 2 hours).  Can continue camera startup, biases, darks, hex warmups, M1M3 bump, HP, laser tracker tests and raise mirror at this time.
  2. Laser tracker M2 Hexapod LUT Test (BLOCK-T401_v4)
  3. Laser tracker Camera Hexapod LUT Spot Check Test (BLOCK-T401_v4)
  4. ONLY if the spot check fails, run the Laser Tracker Camera Hexapod LUT Test (BLOCK-T436_v4)
  5. If spot check succeeds, we go on-sky. We need to enable hexapods with laser_rotation_elevation_v19.yaml. Compensation mode ON.
  6. Run close loop (at least 10 iterations). (BLOCK-T539_hexapods) 10 iterations with configuration (10,5), to make sure we fix the hexapods first, since we are starting with a new LUT configurations. Run for more iterations or until the correction does not improve any further.
  7. Run close loop (at least 10 iterations). (BLOCK-T539) 10 iterations with configuration (22,12), or until the correction does not improve any further.
  8. If no gradient is observed, do a check of the new LUT as a function of elevation and rotation angle ~30 / 40 min (BLOCK-T395).
  9. Stability test (2 hours) (BLOCK-T614)
  10. If seeing is bad (>1.3"), do BLOCK-T624 pre-LSST survey
  11. Close dome at 4:35am CLT (and close the louvers) and do BLOCK-T399: Daily cals.
  12. Everything in park position at end of night. Point at horizon. Close mirror covers.

We should be running both DIMMs and should be ready for tonight, keep an eye on them from time to time (all are displayed in "Environment" chronograf dashboard).  Double check the tower dome closes as expected at the end of the night.

AOS is the main priority (alignment, stability, LUT verification) then FBS pre-LSST survey efficiency test is filler at the end of the night.  Close 1 hour before twilight this week to facilitate calibrations.

Note: AOS can tolerate more cloud coverage than pre-LSST survey.  In very poor seeing conditions, consider switching to pre-LSST survey.  Confirm this with AOS scientists.  Rule of thumb for first 2 weeks of campaign: "if delivered image quality better than ~1.3", then do dedicated AOS tests"


In case of poor conditions (bad seeing, not necessarily cloudy):
- BLOCK-T624 pre-LSST survey


Plan Summary - Closed Dome
Closed dome tests focus on calibration.  For Monochromatic Flats, please run i-band and z-band filters. This is the highest closed-dome priority, followed by stray light tests. Both whitelight and monochromatic flats require dark conditions (Sun below -5 deg should be dark enough).

  1. Whitelight Flats: BLOCK-T556. I and z band
  2. BLOCK-T360: mono support tests
  3. Monochromatic Flats: BLOCK-T523. i and z band.  Duration ~40 mins/filter


Cloudy Nights (long duration).  Note that going on sky gets priority (abandon it if sky gets clear while taking flats).
  1. PTC Curve: BLOCK-T563.  Needs to start at the very beginning of the night and run all night long




Stray Light in-dome tests available:
- none defined yet.

M1M3/TMA tests are lower priority than calibrations and stray light. 
However, they can be ran during the day. 
Confirm with Petr to run with 20%, only GGGG.
Follow the sequence of tests in the Test Player. 

Other Status
  • Filters available: only i, z and pinhole
  • For tonight, we are using the following configuration for CamHex and M2Hexapod:  
    CameraHex: laser_rotation_elevation_v18.yaml
    M2Hex: laser_rotation_elevation_v18.yaml


____________________________________________________________________________________
Homing the axes with home_both_axes.py script

  • To improve homing accuracy and ensure axes homing is done at a consistent az/el location,
    we have added a feature to the home_both_axes.py script that will first home the axes in its current location (as usual),
    then slew the TMA to a fixed position in az/el and perform the homing again.
    This should be run every time you need to home the axes, 
    including after recovering from a TMA fault. 
    Note that the MTPtg Component must be ENABLED in order to command the slew to the final home position. 

  • The feature can be enabled by adding the following configuration to the home_both_axes.py script:
    We want to keep the position az:1, el: 46 for this.
    This position was chosen as it is in the middle of both axes ranges. 


final_home_position: 
  az: 1 
  el: 46

Dome Warming Procedure (likely not needed in Spring):
  1. Close dome
  2. Set HVAC setpoints to high (15 - 20C)
  3. Also have @Petr Kubánek or @Brian Stalder online to adjust the M1M3 setpoint. 
    Need to confirm with Petr that it is working as expected, but some automation is in place. 
  4. CAVEAT: Once we are closed due to cold weather (and heating the dome), 
    even if it warms up OUTSIDE, we do NOT re-open the dome for on-sky that same night

M1M3 status
  • Need to move TMA in 5% speed using EUI if mirror is lowered.
  • Mirror raising/lowering
  • Raising the mirror can be done for El > 20 deg
  • Lowering the mirror can be done El > 45 deg (due to OBS-1038)
  • M1M3 switched back to "enabled HP corrections after raise"
  • 10% GGGR
  • If M1M3 faults itself (i.e. not driven by an interlock) during a slew or tracking, run bump test -> HP breakaway test again before raising mirror again

Pre-Night Checklist / Reminders

  2. No need to wait for sunset to vent the dome.  This is to avoid large thermal differentials and gradients when attempting AOS alignment at the start of observations. Instructions are:
    • wind and humidity conditions are favorable
    • outside air temperature (ESS:301), is at or below inside air temperature (ESS:112)
    • point dome 90 +/- 45, so between 45 and 135 azimuth
    • vent with both the available louvers and shutter
    • if any of the louvers allow sunlight through to shine on the telescope, close those specific ones.
    • mirror covers should remain closed until minus 5 degree sun alt


  3. Check the M2Hexapod acceleration before going on sky. 
    Should be 100 microns/s^2. Check this dashboard.
     
  4. New dashboard for image vignetting.
    It determines whether data is embargoed or not for calibration.
    When taking calibration data, stop if not fully vignetted.
    Problem must be fixed before continuing

  5. Scheduler - runs out of targets. Something is wrong, not normal.
    Ask for support to verify the cause.

  6. If M1M3, M2, or Hexapods go into fault during on-sky observations:
    1. Enable CSCs and Hexapod Compensation Mode.
    2. Critically important: Run set_dof using a previous image with good image quality.

  7. We should be running the Tower DIMM (1). and Portable DIMM (2). Keep an eye from time to time. 
    All are displayed in "Environment" chronograf dashboard.  
    Double check the tower dome closes as expected at the end of the night.

  8. AOS can tolerate more cloud coverage than pre-LSST survey.  
    In very poor seeing conditions, consider switching to pre-LSST survey.  
    Confirm this with AOS scientists.
    Rule of thumb for first 2 weeks of campaign: 
    "if delivered image quality better than ~1.3", then do dedicated AOS tests"

  9. Close dome at start of Astronomical Twilight. 
    We are pointing away from sunrise three hours before closing.
    Start daily calibrations.

  10. If there's an error during calibrations, check to see if it is the issue with changing the filter (OBS-1360).
    There's a recovery procedure to mitigate this issue https://rubinobs.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OOD/pages/1144684545/FES+Filter+change+ends+in+error+with+a+timeout+of+the+Lock+Unlock+of+the+Mount+Rotator

Night conditions

On-Sky Plan Summary
  • We are operating at GGGG tonight.

  • BLOCK-T464 - Start venting as soon as the outdoor temperature is below the indoor temperature.
    Vent pointing 90º away from to the wind.
     
  • BLOCK-T618 - Open the louver and leave it open all night.

  • We need to enable hexapods with default configuration for tonight.
    Compensation mode ON.

Potential ToO (to be confirmed)
If the ToO is triggered, it becomes the highest priority and should be executed when available.

AOS Tests
AOS is the main priority. Expect it to take a little over half of the night, with remaining time for FBS Observations until the end of the night. 
  • BLOCK-T539 Initial Alignment
  • BLOCK-T640 Kick the Robot (~2hrs)
  • BLOCK-T559 Filter Offsets Test (~1hr). Please run this test for g_6 and i_39 filters only. 
  • BLOCK-T614 Stability Test at one position pointing into wind (if possible)

If there are changes to the MTAOS, be sure to run:
  • BLOCK-T539 Initial Alignment
  • BLOCK-T614 Stability Test at one position pointing into wind (if possible)

FBS Observations
We have two configurations available.  
  • Observations scheduled independent of environment conditions to provide an unbiased sampling of the system performance --> USE BLOCK-T624
  • Observations triggered by environmental conditions that are not suitable for other tests (e.g., not meeting atmosphere seeing criteria to be suitable for dedicated AOS tests) --> USE BLOCK-T630
  • If there is fault during FBS observations, make sure you run maintel/ensure_onsky_readiness.py before resuming observations. The Script has to succeed before resuming. 

Priorities for Poor Seeing Conditions:
If seeing conditions are poor (> 1.3 arcsec) consider the following tests in order of priority:
  • BLOCK-T599: LSSTCam Stray Light from Filters Shiny Plate NOTE this cannot tolerate cloudy conditions. 
  • BLOCK-T630: FBS Poor Seeing

End of Night
Once we close, prioritize the following tests. Remember, for calibrations turn laser tracker on as soon as observations stop to minimize time.
  • Please run BLOCK-T556 WhileLightFlats in the u-band only instead of daily calibrations. It should take about the same time. 
  • If you are unable to run calibrations, please instead run the 20% Dynamic Tests. BE SURE TO USE Version 5.0 of all of these test cases:
    • BLOCK-T231: TMA Azimuth Brake Distance - 20% Settings GGGG
    • BLOCK-T240: TMA Elevation Brake Distance - 20% Settings GGGG
    • BLOCK-T241: M2 closed-loop break-out brake test during TMA slew - 20% Settings GGGG

____________________________________________________________________________
Closed Dome Plan Summary
Closed dome tests focus on calibration. 

If you will be closed all night (or at least 6hrs), prioritize running:
  • BLOCK-T563: 750 pair PTC curve

If you get longer closed dome conditions:
  • 20% Dynamic Tests are available. BE SURE TO USE Version 5.0 of all of these test cases:
    • BLOCK-T231: TMA Azimuth Brake Distance - 20% Settings GGGG
    • BLOCK-T240: TMA Elevation Brake Distance - 20% Settings GGGG
    • BLOCK-T241: M2 closed-loop break-out brake test during TMA slew - 20% Settings GGGG
  • Whitelight flats (BLOCK-T556): u,z,i,r,g

Other Status
  • Filters available:  i, z, g, r, u
  • For tonight, we are using the following configuration for CamHex and M2Hexapod:  
    CameraHex: default configuration
    M2Hex: default configuration

M1M3 status
  • Need to move TMA in 5% speed using EUI if mirror is lowered.
  • Mirror raising/lowering
  • Raising the mirror can be done for El > 45 deg. Do not raise below 45 deg.
  • Lowering the mirror can be done El > 40 deg (due to OBS-1038). Do not lower below 40 deg. 
  • TMA can be slewed to horizon while M1M3 is raised. M1M3 can stay raised at horizon during the day, do not lower it. 
  • 10% GGGG

  • SITCOM Test Planning - Canvas with the priorities of the Week
  • OBS-965 TMA Azimuth Encoders - Fault & cleaning log: Take notes of Az positions on any encoder head losses or faults.
  • If there is fault during FBS observations: 
    • Make sure you run maintel/ensure_onsky_readiness.py before resuming observations. The Script has to succeed before resuming.
    • Critically important: Run set_dof using a previous image with good image quality.
  • Default TMA settings are now same as 20percentperformance.
    We should be monitoring the max HP forces are in the expected range (around or below 1000N): M1M3 TMA Inertial forces - min max

Announcement: https://rubin-obs.slack.com/archives/C07QCJ7F962/p1765398509913509
  • Closing the dome aperture at Nautical Twilight (-12 degrees) instead of Astronomical Twilight (-18 degrees). 
  • Azimuth constraint in the last 3 hours has been removed (except when running on generator power). 
  • In the event of a complete power failure in the night/morning - call everyone as per Management Emergency Squadcast Form.

OBS-1479 Update on Dewpoint Criteria
  • Before opening, check if the dewpoint from the weather tower is 2ºC lower than Dynalene temperature and perform a visual inspection before opening the mirror covers. 
  • MTDome Weather Monitor - Close if the difference between dynalene/glycol and outside dewpoint is smaller than 2ºC for ~ 20 min.
  • Request to go up and do a visual inspection looking for water drops/condensation.
    Perform only if you need to close the dome shutter and/or in the morning next day.
    • Record in the Night Log: time, dew point top-end (ESS:111), dew point outside (ESS:301), dynalene temperature at mirror level ( lsst.MTCamera.utiltrunk_ut.CoolPipeSplyTemp- 1.5ºC), decision.

On-Sky Plan Summary
Listed by priority here and in test plan.

Note that v23 LUT has been made default (NCWE is also default).
See announcement: https://rubin-obs.slack.com/archives/C07Q45P0PAB/p1766164443180349.
No test-case in the plan for tonight should use any other configuration.

All day closed-dome calibrations (During the day):
Daytime calibrations (closed-dome, lights off)
  • Darks (38s darks): BLOCK-T485.  We want 200+, preferably 400.  These are optional; we aren’t using them at the moment.  We can take them opportunistically in the future.  This can be done after 30s darks or during the day if the lights are off. (do this during the day time)


On Sky:
  • BLOCK-T674: Simonyi LSSTCam Feature Based Scheduler LSST Survey (with Closed-Loop on Filter Change)
    • config: "fbs_config_lsst_survey_block_419.yaml"
    • No rotator angle constraint
    • No altitude constraint
    • No filter constraints
    • Expect multi-band images taken tonight. Images taken after filter changes will be a bit slower to allow for additional MTAOS closed-loop iterations. 

In-Dome (If we have to close the dome)
BLOCK-T566 1.0 CBP No Filter Sweep
BLOCK-339 3.0 CBP Filter Sweep

End of night
  • No specific requests, all-night calibrations

name: 2026-01-13 Pre-LSST Campaign Plan
description:
Temporary Guidelines - LSSTCam on-sky
  • SITCOM Test Planning - Canvas with the priorities of the Week
  • OBS-965 TMA Azimuth Encoders - Fault & cleaning log: Take notes of Az positions on any encoder head losses or faults.
  • If there is fault during FBS observations: 
    • Make sure you run maintel/ensure_onsky_readiness.py before resuming observations. The Script has to succeed before resuming.
    • Critically important: Run set_dof using a previous image with good image quality.
  • Default TMA settings are now same as 20percentperformance.
    We should be monitoring the max HP forces are in the expected range (around or below 1000N): M1M3 TMA Inertial forces - min max

Announcement: https://rubin-obs.slack.com/archives/C07QCJ7F962/p1765398509913509
  • Closing the dome aperture at Nautical Twilight (-12 degrees) instead of Astronomical Twilight (-18 degrees). 
  • Azimuth constraint in the last 3 hours has been removed (except when running on generator power). 
  • In the event of a complete power failure in the night/morning - call everyone as per Management Emergency Squadcast Form.

OBS-1479 Update on Dewpoint Criteria
  • Before opening, check if the dewpoint from the weather tower is 2ºC lower than Dynalene temperature and perform a visual inspection before opening the mirror covers. 
  • MTDome Weather Monitor - Close if the difference between dynalene/glycol and outside dewpoint is smaller than 2ºC for ~ 20 min.
  • Request to go up and do a visual inspection looking for water drops/condensation.
    Perform only if you need to close the dome shutter and/or in the morning next day.
    • Record in the Night Log: time, dew point top-end (ESS:111), dew point outside (ESS:301), dynalene temperature at mirror level (lsst.MTCamera.utiltrunk_ut.CoolPipeSplyTemp- 1.5ºC), decision.

On-Sky Plan Summary
Plan is to continue FBS pre-LSST observations tonight. 
Listed by priority here and in test plan.

On Sky:
  • BLOCK-T674: Simonyi LSSTCam Feature Based Scheduler LSST Survey (with Closed-Loop on Filter Change)
    • config: "fbs_config_lsst_survey_block_419.yaml"
    • No rotator angle constraint
    • No altitude constraint
    • No filter constraints
    • Expect multi-band images taken tonight. Images taken after filter changes will be a bit slower to allow for additional MTAOS closed-loop iterations.
  • BLOCK-T429: LSSTCam stray light from M2 baffle using the Moon (30 min)
    • Prepare in advance to start it at sharp at 5:00 AM CLT.
    • Gabriele and Alessio will be connected to support it.
    • It requires careful monitoring of the HV bias current to prevent any tripping, although not expected.
      Already proven to be safe during the ChaosMonkey Moon approach

In-Dome (If we have to close the dome) - 
If there is a violation of the requirement that the dew point temp. must be 2 deg C colder than the dynalene temp., we must park the TMA at horizon.  No closed dome tests can be performed until a visual inspection has been performed and there are no signs of dripping. 

  • No specific requests, usual minimal calibrations

End of night
  • No specific requests, usual minimal calibrations

customFields.Requests for the end of the night: TMA at Zenith for M1M3 work (Franco C. Jan.13)

OBS-1479 Update on Dewpoint Criteria
  • Before opening, check if the dewpoint from the weather tower is 2ºC lower than Dynalene temperature and perform a visual inspection before opening the mirror covers.

  • Request to go up and do a visual inspection looking for water drops/condensation.
    Perform only if you need to close the dome shutter and/or in the morning next day.
    • Record in the Night Log: time, dew point top-end (ESS:111), dew point outside (ESS:301), dynalene temperature at mirror level (lsst.MTCamera.utiltrunk_ut.CoolPipeSplyTemp- 1.5ºC), decision.

Running on Generator (Wed/Thu nights):
  • Use fbs_config_limited_lsst_survey_on_generator.py (it automatically kicks azimuth constraints 3 hours before sunrise)
  • 3 hours before Sunrise:
    • TMA should remain in -45° < Az < -90° if running dedicated tests.

On-Sky Plan Summary
Plan is to continue FBS pre-LSST observations tonight. 
Switch to "on generator" FBS version 3 hours before Sunrise.
Listed by priority here and in test plan.

On Sky:
  • BLOCK-T539 (Initial alignment):
    • Updated to have 5 iterations in total now:
      • 2 iterations with closed_loop_hexapods_10dof_trunc5 (hexapods only)
      • 3 iterartion with close_loop_22dof_trunc12
  • BLOCK-T674: Simonyi LSSTCam Feature Based Scheduler LSST Survey (Closed-Loop on Filter Change)
    • Run the "on generator" config version of block_419 config: 
      • config: "fbs_config_lsst_survey_block_419_on_generator.yaml"
      • No rotator angle constraint
      • No altitude constraint
      • No filter constraints
      • "On generator" version automatically kicks azimuth constraints 3 hours before sunrise
    • Expect multi-band images taken. Images taken after filter changes will be a bit slower to allow for additional MTAOS closed-loop iterations.
  • BLOCK-T540: LSSTCam stray light off-axis angular extent of banana features (40 min) 
    • Run this if we have bad IQ (> 2.0"). No clouds.
    • Not time critical, but it cannot be executed in the last 3 hours due to Azimuth restrictions (on generator).

Closed Dome (If we have to close the dome) - 
If there is a violation of the requirement that the dew point temp (must be 1.0 deg C colder than the dynalene temp.), we must park the TMA at horizon.  No closed dome tests can be performed until a visual inspection has been performed and there are no signs of dripping. 
  • BLOCK-T595: LSSTCam scratched tape stray light path using CBP (< 1 hour).
  • No other specific requests, just the usual minimal calibrations

End of night
  • No specific requests, usual minimal calibrations

name: 2026-01-20 Pre-LSST Campaign Plan
description:
SITCOM Test Planning - Canvas with the priorities of the Week

OBS-965 TMA Azimuth Encoders - Fault & cleaning log: Take notes of Az positions on any encoder head losses or faults.
  • If there is fault during FBS observations: 
    • Make sure you run maintel/ensure_onsky_readiness.py before resuming observations. The Script has to succeed before resuming.
    • Critically important: Run set_dof using a previous image with good image quality.
  • Default TMA settings are now same as 20percentperformance.
    We should be monitoring the max HP forces are in the expected range (around or below 1000N): M1M3 TMA Inertial forces - min max

OBS-1479 Update on Dewpoint Criteria
  • Before opening, check if the dewpoint from the weather tower is no more than 2 ºC higher than the Dynalene temperature and perform a visual inspection before opening the mirror covers. 
  • MTDome Weather Monitor - Close if the difference between dynalene/glycol and outside dewpoint is smaller than -2.0 ºC for ~ 20 min. 
  • Request to go up and do a visual inspection looking for water drops/condensation.
    Perform only if you need to close the dome shutter and/or in the morning next day.
    • Record in the Night Log: time, dew point top-end (ESS:111), dew point outside (ESS:301), dynalene temperature at mirror level (lsst.MTCamera.utiltrunk_ut.CoolPipeSplyTemp- 1.5ºC), decision.

On-Sky Plan Summary
Camera running at -102 ºC (non-usual). 
Camera cannot keep the temperature when the telescope is at Zenith and will likely lose control during the night.
We can observe, but we cannot park the telescope at Zenith. 

Friendly reminder to use OBS-1523 for tracking time loss when closed due to the difference between dew point and dynalene temperatures.

Late Afternoon
  • BLOCK-T88v3 - Run before going on Sky - Aim for ~ 1.5h before initial alignment.
    It might be more efficient to run this test even before opening the dome shutter. 
    If possible, keel the same Az/El where you will start the night. Or, at least, El. 
    This test will take ~ 45 min. Prioritize going on sky if needed. 
    If we run this, skip Step 1 of BLOCK-T539 which will reset the DOFs to 0.

On Sky:
  • BLOCK-T539: Initial alignment
    • Updated to have 5 iterations in total now:
      • 2 iterations with closed_loop_hexapods_10dof_trunc5 (hexapods only) - These interactions will always run in the JSON Block.
      • 3 iterations with close_loop_22dof_trunc12 - These interactions are reflected in the JSON Block configuration.
  • BLOCK-T674: Simonyi LSSTCam Feature Based Scheduler LSST Survey (with Closed-Loop on Filter Change)
    • config: "fbs_config_lsst_survey_block_419.yaml"
    • We are running a new version of BLOCK-T632: Setup FBS to use truncation index = 11 instead of 12 on Step 3. 
      This is already updated in the test execution. 
      This means a change in the maintel/enable_aos_closed_loop.py script configuration.

Very Poor Seeing (> 2.0"):
The FBS can continue to be run in poor seeing, but the following tests will have higher value and ​should ​be considered. Once completed, ​you can return to FBS observations. 
  • BLOCK-T540: LSSTCam stray light off-axis angular extent of banana features (40 min) 
    • Run this if we have bad IQ (> 2.0"). No clouds.
    • Not time critical, but it cannot be executed in the last 3 hours due to Azimuth restrictions (on generator).

Closed Dome 
If there is a violation of the requirement that the dew point temp (must be 1.0 deg C colder than the dynalene temp.), 
we must park the TMA at horizon.  
No closed dome tests can be performed until a visual inspection has been performed and there are no signs of dripping. 
  • BLOCK-T595: LSSTCam scratched tape stray light path using CBP (< 1 hour).

End of night
  • BLOCK-T664: Minimal Daily Cals
    Move the telescope to Horizon after cals.

A temporary HVAC procedure is in place for the night crew at the end of the night only while glycol flow is low. - PoC Kevin F.

This is to avoid risk to the PCS chiller tripping, causing a camera warmup (or worse):

  1. Before closing the dome, send EAS to STANDBY.

  2. Close the dome normally.

  3. Turn on AHUs one at a time excluding AHU2, taking a ~5 min pause between monitoring chiller/Maq20/ on big plot (switch to an hour scale)

    1. GlycInputFlow should stay above 2gpm

    2. GlycChillerIn should not raise significantly when turning on an AHU

    3. Stg2DeSuHtrOut should remain below 30°C

    4. GlycChillerOut should remain below 30°C

    5. These parameters are related, and likely these all happen together.

  4. It is very possible you will only be able to turn on one or two AHU.

  5. Turn on AHU2 (this is valved off to glycol - so should have no effect).
